name: The match factory by St. Paul's, Mather Street

function.note: The fire went 'into the high church, at the corner of Clinton and Mather streets, and thence to the match factory and Bateham's planing mills' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 716).

built.note: Not known: reconstructed as standing through the later 1860s.

research_note: THE MATCH FACTORY, built by T-3831: the match factory the fire reached from the church on its way to Bateham's mills (Andreas vol. 2, p. 716); Engine 14's foreman laid a line of hose 'between the mill and church and match factory' (p. 717). Whose it was, its size and its form are not recorded: a two-storey frame factory on Mather Street between the church and the mills, reconstructed.

documented_range.note: Standing on the night of the fire (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 716-717); when it was built is not known.

position.symbolic_location: Mather Street, north side, between St. Paul's church and Bateham's mills.
position.note: Andreas puts it between the church and the mills (pp. 716-717); its place on Mather Street in that gap is reconstructed. The footprint's origin is local E -213.5 N -1531.0; the frame is turned onto the 1871 plan's grid.

derivation.reason: Laid out from Andreas's description of the block against the 1871 plan's Clinton and Canal streets and the line of Mather Street; no traced frontage for the 1871 city is in data/traces/street_control.json to recompute it from.

footprint.note: Its size is not recorded; reconstructed to fill the gap between the church and the west mill.

value.note: THE MATCH FACTORY, built by T-3831.

fire.note: Burned between the church and the mills (Andreas vol. 2, p. 716).

composition.note: Not described in any account read: reconstructed whole.

wall_material.value: Sawn boards on a frame, a shingle roof
wall_material.note: Not stated: taken to be frame, as its neighbours were.

phases.change_note: Built T-3831 (2026-11-28): the match factory between the church and the mills.
